title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: Including the QLD Teacher Salary Example
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. See how the QLD teacher salary compares to national averages and understand tax and super.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by hours per week (assumed 38) times 52 weeks, with super paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. Adjust the weekly hours if you work a different pattern.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 with casual loading. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations and are typically higher. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for your correct minimum rate.

faqs.q: Does the QLD teacher salary example include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, the example shows gross salary before super. The super guarantee requires your employer to pay an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. So if your gross annual salary is $98,800, your employer contributes about $11,856 in super on top.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare pay across different roles. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For full-time employees, we typically assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly.

For example, an hourly rate of $40 gives an annual gross of $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. Your fortnightly pay would be roughly $3,040 before tax and super.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid on top of the base rate, so never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the timesheet.

Many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 2026–27), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Average weekly earnings vary across states. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings survey for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings nationally were $2,083.70 per week. In Queensland, the figure was $2,039.70 per week. These are averages across all industries and occupations, not medians for any specific job. They give a useful benchmark but do not represent a particular role like teaching.

## The QLD Teacher Salary in Context

When considering the QLD teacher salary, it's important to note that teachers are typically covered by an award or enterprise agreement. The average weekly earnings for full-time workers in Queensland is $2,039.70, but this is an average across all industries and occupations, not the median for teachers. To estimate annual pay for a teacher earning a given hourly rate, use the formula.

Suppose a Queensland teacher earns $50 per hour under their agreement. Their annual gross would be $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. Fortnightly, that is about $3,800 before tax. Super at 12% adds $11,856 on top, making the total package $110,656. Remember that actual pay may differ due to step increments, allowances, or negotiated conditions.

## Tax and Superannuation

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. The tax-free threshold is included. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means your total remuneration package is higher than your gross salary.

## Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It calculates annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, along with estimated tax and super. For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) for up-to-date minimums.

Remember that this is an estimate. Your actual pay may vary based on your award, agreement, hours, and personal tax situation. Always consult a qualified professional for binding advice.
